events.text: During this watch session for patient P3, adhesions obscured Calot's triangle at the start, and 15 frames were held back due to obscured views or perception errors. Multiple safety alerts were triggered at t=409, t=415, and t=517, including cutting without two clips, clipping before achieving the Critical View of Safety (CVS), and a common bile duct (CBD) injury alert. All safety alerts were automatically acknowledged by the system due to the recording mode. Throughout the session (from t=411 to t=561), numerous verification contradictions occurred, indicating premature phase transitions to gallbladder dissection, premature marking of structures as skeletonised or cut despite ongoing dissection and clipping, and inflated clip counts. The session concluded in the gallbladder-dissection phase with an incomplete CVS (2/3), the CBD marked as at risk, the cystic duct recorded as cut with 6 clips, and the cystic artery clipped with 5 clips.
key_events: t=409: Alerts triggered and auto-acknowledged for cutting without two clips, clipping before CVS, and CBD injury.
t=415 & t=517: Repeat alerts triggered and auto-acknowledged for clipping before CVS.

t=411–t=531: Multiple verification contradictions flagged for prematurely marking the gallbladder and cystic plate as skeletonised and the cystic duct as cut while dissection and clipping were still ongoing.

t=561: Verification contradictions noted an impossible sequence of dissecting and clipping the cystic duct after it was marked cut, as well as excessive clip counts (6 on duct, 5 on artery) from frame-counting errors.
End of session: 15 frames held back; final state reached gallbladder-dissection with CVS at 2/3 and CBD at risk.
